name: Play AccessibilityService API policy
plain: Accessibility services see and control the screen, so Play limits them to real accessibility use.
meaning: A powerful hook used by malware for fraud. Play requires a declaration and bars use for call recording, ads or remote control unless the app is an accessibility tool.

android.prompt_ui: User enables it in Settings > Accessibility with a warning
android.store_policy: AccessibilityService API policy; isAccessibilityTool flag; declaration form; disclosure required
android.note: Android 13 blocks Restricted settings for sideloaded apps.

ios.api_surface: UIAccessibility APIs for the app's own UI only
ios.note: No equivalent system wide control; Switch Control is user side.

limits.headline: Can see and control your screen once you turn it on in Settings
limits.user_action: You go to Settings, then Accessibility, switch the app on, and accept a warning
can: See what is on screen and tap buttons for you, for people who need that help
Speak screen text aloud or fill in forms, for accessibility tools
Help control the phone with a keyboard or switch
cannot: Switch itself on without your steps in Settings
Be used on Play for call recording, ads or remote control, unless it is an accessibility tool
Be switched on from a sideloaded app on Android 13 without the Restricted settings step
Work this way on iPhone; Switch Control is a user side tool
limits.differs: Android has this service with a Play policy. iPhone has no equivalent system wide control for apps.

story.what_it_is: Google's rule that limits the powerful screen reading tool to real accessibility apps.

marketing.name: AccessibilityService API policy
marketing.pitch: Only apps that truly help people with disabilities may use this powerful tool, and they must say so.

story.for_you: If you rely on a screen reader or switch control, this is what makes your phone work. For everyone else, it is a wall that stops malicious apps from watching and tapping for you.
story.for_makers: The tool can read the whole screen and press buttons, so crooks used it to steal bank logins. Google requires a declaration, and bars use for call recording, ads or remote control unless the app is truly an accessibility tool.

use_cases.example: A screen reader reads the screen out loud to a blind user and lets them navigate by touch.
Banking apps detect an accessibility service that does not belong, and block high risk actions.
A game macro tool used the service to auto tap, which Play now bans for cheating.
A password manager uses the service as a fallback to fill logins in apps that do not support autofill.
An ad app tried to click on ads for you in the background, and Play bans that use.
A remote support tool for company phones needs a special approval and a clear on screen notice.

story.android_note: This is an Android only service and a favorite of malware, so Android 13 added a restricted settings gate.
story.ios_note: iOS has no match. Its assistive features are built in and apps cannot read other apps' screens.

history.change: Restricted settings for sideloaded accessibility services
